title: Tortellini with Butternut Squash

2 servings: 1/4 small onion, chopped, or 1 clove garlic
3 Tbsp grated Parmesan - optional, see notes for the dairy-free version
Salt, and a small squeeze of lemon at the end
4 servings: 1/2 small onion, chopped, or 2 cloves garlic
1/3 cup grated Parmesan - optional, see notes for the dairy-free version
Salt, and a squeeze of lemon at the end

steps: Heat the oven to 425F. Toss the squash with the olive oil and a good pinch of salt and spread it in a single layer on a sheet pan - crowded squash steams instead of browning. Roast until the edges are genuinely caramelized: 25-30 min for 1-inch pieces, 20-25 min for 2/3-inch cubes, flipping once around the 15-minute mark. Add the chopped onion to the pan for the last 15 min.
Boil the tortellini from frozen while the squash finishes. RESERVE 1 CUP of the pasta water before draining.

Blend the roasted squash and onion with the stock, butter, nutmeg, the Parmesan if using, and about 1/2 cup of the pasta water until completely smooth - 45 seconds, longer than feels necessary. Any texture left is what a kid will find.
Taste and salt properly, then add a small squeeze of lemon - it lifts the whole thing out of flat-and-sweet.
Toss with the drained tortellini over low heat for a minute, thinning with more pasta water a splash at a time until the sauce coats rather than clumps.
notes: ROAST, DO NOT BOIL. Boiled squash tastes like baby food - watery and flat. The caramelized edges are where all the sweetness comes from, and the sweetness is the whole reason kids eat this. In a hurry, microwave it covered with 2 Tbsp water for 8 min and stir in 1 tsp of honey to make up for what you lost. ROASTING TIME IS ABOUT PIECE SIZE, NOT QUANTITY - a third of a cup and three cups take the same time. 1-inch pieces 25-30 min at 425F, 2/3-inch cubes 20-25 min, check at 18. For a small amount use a small pan or a toaster oven; a few cubes on a big hot sheet pan scorch at the edges before the centres soften. If the edges are browning but the centres are still firm, drop to 375F for another 5-8 min. FOR A YOUNG KID, cook past fork-tender to genuinely mashable - it should squash with light pressure between your fingers. Firm cubes are a choking risk, and a toddler rejects a texture before she ever gets to the flavour. PASTA WATER, NOT MORE STOCK, for thinning. The starch is what makes it cling to the tortellini instead of sliding off into a puddle. Reserve it before you drain - everyone forgets. DAIRY-FREE / NO CHEESE: skip the Parmesan and use 1-2 Tbsp nutritional yeast (closest to a cheesy flavour), or 1 tsp white miso or 1/2 tsp soy sauce for the savoury edge. Keep the butter, or swap it for olive oil plus 1 Tbsp tahini. Then salt it properly - most 'tastes flat without cheese' is actually under-salting. WHAT ELSE CAN GO IN: roasted carrot or sweet potato (more sweetness, same colour); cauliflower, roasted on the same pan (disappears completely); a jarred roasted red pepper blended in at the end (deeper, slightly smoky). Spinach or peas work but turn the sauce green instead of orange - fine if your kids do not care about colour, a dealbreaker if they do. FOR THE ADULTS: brown a tablespoon of butter with a few sage leaves and spoon it over the top, plus black pepper and chilli flakes. Keeps the kids' bowls plain. FREEZES WELL - the sauce on its own, not with the pasta in it. Roast a whole bag of squash, make a double batch of sauce and freeze half in a jar; it is a 10-minute dinner later. Thin with water when reheating, it sets up thick in the fridge.

title: Broccoli, Butternut Squash & Lentils (No Cheese)
servings: about 6 kid portions (batch cooks and freezes)
source: Variation on Tiny Tums Recipes (@tinytumsrecipes), de-cheesed
ingredients: 150 g dry brown lentils (3/4 cup) - or red lentils, see notes
600 ml low-salt chicken or vegetable stock (about 2 1/2 cups)
1 cup butternut squash, peeled and finely grated (or diced very small)
1 cup broccoli florets, chopped very fine (pea-sized)
1 Tbsp butter or olive oil, stirred in at the end - replaces the fat the cheese was bringing
INSTEAD OF THE CHEESE, pick one: 1-2 Tbsp nutritional yeast, or 1 tsp white (shiro) miso, or 1/2 tsp soy sauce, or 1 Tbsp tahini
ADD-INS, pick one or two, about 1 cup total: grated carrot; finely diced sweet potato; finely chopped cauliflower; 1 jarred roasted red pepper, chopped
steps: Rinse the lentils and pick out any small stones or shriveled ones.

Heat the oil in a pot over medium. Add the garlic and squash and saute 3-4 min, until the squash softens and the garlic is fragrant. GRATED CARROT and DICED SWEET POTATO go in here too, with the squash.
Add the lentils and all the stock. Bring to a boil, then simmer 18-20 min.

Add the broccoli and simmer 8-10 min more, stirring now and then, until the lentils and broccoli are very soft - 25-30 min total for the lentils. CHOPPED CAULIFLOWER goes in here, with the broccoli. Add a splash of water if it dries out.

Take it off the heat. Stir in the butter, then the nutritional yeast, miso, soy sauce or tahini. CHOPPED ROASTED RED PEPPER goes in now, off the heat - it is already cooked and simmering it just turns it to mush.
Mash with a fork to the texture she likes, loose or smooth. Taste it yourself before serving.
notes: NO CHEESE. The cheddar was doing four jobs and each has a replacement. FAT - the tablespoon of butter or oil stirred in off the heat; this is the one not to skip, it is what keeps it from tasting lean and watery. UMAMI - 1-2 Tbsp nutritional yeast is the closest thing to a cheesy flavour and has no salt, which matters under 2; 1 tsp white miso or 1/2 tsp soy sauce both work and are more savoury than cheesy; 1 Tbsp tahini gives richness and a little nuttiness. BODY - the lentils already do this, which is why this recipe misses the cheese far less than the orzo version does. SALT - for an older kid or an adult bowl, salt it at the end; most 'tastes flat without cheese' is actually under-salting. Miso, soy and tahini all bring salt, so for under 1 use the nutritional yeast or none of them. WHEN EACH ADD-IN GOES IN - this is the part that matters. GRATED CARROT and FINELY DICED SWEET POTATO go in at the start with the squash; they need the full cook, add sweetness, and keep the orange colour. FINELY CHOPPED CAULIFLOWER goes in with the broccoli for the last 8-10 min; it disappears completely into the mash and is the most invisible vegetable of the four. JARRED ROASTED RED PEPPER goes in at the very end, off the heat - it is already cooked, it only needs to warm through, and simmering it turns it to slurry. It is the biggest flavour change of the four: deeper and slightly smoky. ROASTED CARROT instead of grated is better still if the oven is already on - roast it alongside anything else and stir it in at the end. Keep add-ins to about 1 cup total or you throw off the lentil-to-liquid ratio and it goes soupy; add a splash more stock if you go heavier. AVOID SPINACH AND PEAS unless you do not mind the colour - they turn the whole thing muddy green instead of orange. LENTILS: brown lentils hold a little shape, which is fine if you are mashing. Red lentils collapse completely in about 15 min for a smoother, more sauce-like result - cut the stock to about 500 ml and the simmer to 15 min if you use them. MASHABLE SOFT is the bar for a toddler, not fork-tender; the lentils, broccoli and squash should all squash with light pressure. Lentils are high in fibre, so start with smaller portions. The squash is sauteed first for flavour and melts into the lentils; the broccoli goes in last so it stays green and does not turn sulfury. Pre-cut squash saves the peeling. FREEZE single portions in ice-cube trays and reheat with a splash of water.
